task_title: Tag installers pin the release they install
task_criteria: PROOF: release-cut validation and regression tests enforce that a future vX.Y.Z tag's installer default equals the tag and all documented tag-installer instructions carry an explicit TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION pin. FAILIF: a future-tag simulation or negative control can pass with a stale installer default, or a tag installer instruction remains unpinned.

items.criterion: PROOF: release-cut validation and regression tests enforce that a future vX.Y.Z tag's installer default equals the tag and all documented tag-installer instructions carry an explicit TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION pin. FAILIF: a future-tag simulation or negative control can pass with a stale installer default, or a tag installer instruction remains unpinned.
items.detail: scripts/release-cut-check.sh:148-170 compares the prospective tag with install.sh's extracted default, and .github/workflows/release.yml:112-129 repeats the check on the checked-out tag before build/publish. tests/test_release_workflow.py:645-670 executes a matching v9.9.9 candidate; lines 672-724 commit a stale 9.9.8 installer default and require rc=1 with the found/expected mismatch named. tests/test_docs_tag_pins.py:45-49,119-182 scans all three documented instruction surfaces fail-closed; lines 185-214 and 217-261 execute unpinned mutations, including quickstart's prose-declared tag-checkout fence. Fresh focused run exited 0 with `28 passed in 10.95s`; complete test-path legs exited 0 with `2055 passed, 12 skipped` (plugin/) and `199 passed, 3 skipped` (tests/). An independent v9.9.9 docs probe returned rc=1 naming the unpinned instruction and rc=0 after adding TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION=9.9.9. Replaying prior verdict 9c7127c2's exact quickstart pin deletion across all three DOC_PATHS now returns rc=1 naming quickstart.md:95, closing the demonstrated false green. The monolithic suite invocation reached 96% without failure before the 300-second tool timeout; both complete constituent legs then passed.

items.criterion: Coverage seam: every tracked Markdown tag-installer instruction (including README and docs outside the scanner's three hard-coded paths) is either explicitly TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION-pinned or is actually scanned by the regression guard, so no documented tag installer can remain unpinned outside the guard's blind spot.
items.detail: tests/test_docs_tag_pins.py:45-49 covers docs/releasing.md, docs/quickstart.md, and docs/deploy-to-karahermes.md. Repository-wide searches for tag checkouts, `tag checkout` prose, and release-download tag URLs found tag-install instructions only at docs/quickstart.md:88-95 and docs/deploy-to-karahermes.md:60-66; their commands are explicitly pinned at quickstart.md:95 and deploy-to-karahermes.md:66. README.md:214-215 documents release mode rather than a tag checkout, and its older-tag example is pinned. Running the real scanner over all 71 root/docs Markdown files returned `scanned_paths=71 instructions=2 rc=0` with no violations, so no unpinned documented tag installer was found outside the configured paths.

items.criterion: Failure-path integrity: the prospective-tag gate and tag-publish workflow both use the same fail-closed installer-default extraction, and a missing, malformed, or stale installer default cannot produce a successful release-cut/publish validation.
items.detail: scripts/installer-default-version.sh:19-40 refuses missing files and absent, wrong-form, empty, or unparseable pins. scripts/release-cut-check.sh:158-170 converts helper failure or mismatch into a counted failure and exits nonzero at lines 222-227; .github/workflows/release.yml:114-129 exits 1 before build/publish on the same conditions. tests/test_release_workflow.py:174-229 exercises malformed helper inputs and lines 672-724 prove a stale default fails. The focused run exited 0 with 28 passed. Live extraction printed `1.3.4`, matching pyproject.toml:7.

items.criterion: Negative-control strength: the regression suite executes both a matching future-tag simulation and committed stale-installer/unpinned-doc mutations against the real scanners, asserting nonzero status and named mismatch/violation rather than merely checking source text.
items.detail: tests/test_release_workflow.py:645-670 runs the real gate against a matching v9.9.9 fixture; lines 672-724 commit a stale 9.9.8 default and require rc=1 plus `expected 9.9.9` and `wrong assets`. tests/test_docs_tag_pins.py:185-214 injects an unpinned v9.9.8 tag installer into a copy, and lines 217-261 remove only the real quickstart pin; both require nonzero rc, a counted instruction, file:line, and TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION in the violation. Focused pytest exited 0 with `28 passed in 10.95s`. The independent future-tag probe returned `(1, ['future-tag-instruction.md:5: ... lacks an explicit TERMINAL_JAIL_VERSION= pin ...'], 1)` when unpinned and `(0, [], 1)` when pinned.
